title: 'Attack on dissent': UP seeks release of 10 students in ASEAN protests
summary: The premier state university said the incidents threaten academic freedom and the right to dissent.

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 6:16pm

Protesters clash with police officers during a demonstration that coincides with the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Leaders' Summit and Related Summits in Manila on Nov. 15, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — The University of the Philippines Diliman has condemned the arrest of 10 of its students during protests against the US-led Pax Silica initiative and President Donald Trump's planned visit for the ASEAN summit, saying the arrests violated their right to dissent and threatened academic freedom.

In a statement Monday, November 16, the university's Committee on the Protection of Academic Freedom and Human Rights called for the immediate and unconditional release of the students and other protesters arrested during demonstrations over the weekend.
The committee said the students were exercising their right to protest and "oppose policies and agreements they believe serve foreign and corporate interests."

"Their arrest is not merely an attack on individual students but an attack on the people's right to dissent, on academic freedom and on the democratic space that universities have historically defended," the university said.
UP also called for investigations into reports of police abuse during the demonstrations.

"We reiterate our urgent demand: Free the illegally arrested now. End the crackdown on peaceful dissent. Defend democratic rights. The University will continue to stand with its students and the Filipino people and uphold its responsibility to defend academic freedom, human dignity and the people's fundamental rights," the committee said.
Campus journalists also affected
Among those arrested was a staff member of the Philippine Collegian, the official student publication of UP Diliman.
The student journalist was detained along with more than 200 protesters during the Lakbayan ng Timog Katagalugan demonstration in Sucat, Muntinlupa City, on Sunday, November 15.
The student was reportedly still in police custody at Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City as of Monday. The specific complaints or charges against the student have not been disclosed.

In a separate incident, two student journalists from Tinig ng Plaridel, the official publication of UP Diliman's College of Media and Communication, were nearly arrested while covering the All Workers Unity protest march on November 15.

In a joint statement, the college and publication said police verbally intimidated the two journalists and attempted to apprehend them as they documented Manila Police District officers carrying a protester to a police precinct.
One of the journalists sustained minor abrasions during the incident.
Police also confiscated a cellphone containing footage of the protest and arrests.
The Philippine National Police, meanwhile, has defended its handling of the protests, maintaining that officers exercised maximum tolerance before making arrests.
Police said some demonstrators obstructed public roads and refused to comply with authorities, disrupting public order.
Protest groups and campus publications, however, have raised concerns over alleged violations of the rights to peaceful assembly and freedom of the press. — Alyana Uy
